original_question: What is the largest product-free set in the alternating group An ?
target_in_source: Green, 100 Open Problems, Section 1 "Sum-free sets, product-free sets", Problem 4 (page 4)
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the ambient family of groups (the alternating groups A_n) and the extremal question about the largest product-free subset.
missing_details: A_n should be defined as the alternating group of even permutations of {1,...,n}.
"Product-free" should be defined explicitly: a subset A of a group is product-free if there do not exist a,b,c in A with ab=c (equivalently, no solution to a=bc with all three elements in A).
The quantifier over n is missing; the solved primary source formulates the exact result for all sufficiently large n.
It is unclear whether "largest" asks for maximum cardinality, maximum density, or also the classification of the extremal sets.
The source-faithful extremal candidate family should be stated: F_I^x = {pi in A_n : pi(x) in I and pi(I) intersect I is empty}, together with its inverse family.

The draft omits the source context that the problem was already known up to logarithmic factors: Crane-type constructions give density on the order of n^(-1/2), while Eberhard proved an upper bound O(n^(-1/2)(log n)^(7/2)).
The exact resolved formulation includes the qualifier "up to inversion": every maximum-size product-free set is A or A^(-1) for one of the families F_I^x.
refined_question: For each sufficiently large integer n, determine the maximum possible cardinality of a product-free subset A of the alternating group A_n, where product-free means that there do not exist a,b,c in A with ab=c under permutation composition; equivalently, are all maximum-size product-free subsets, up to taking inverses, of the form F_I^x = {pi in A_n : pi(x) in I and pi(I) intersects I is empty} for some x in {1,...,n} and some subset I of {1,...,n}?
equivalent_formulation: For all sufficiently large n, if A is a product-free subset of A_n of maximum cardinality, must there exist x in {1,...,n} and I subseteq {1,...,n} such that either A = {pi in A_n : pi(x) in I and pi(I) intersects I is empty} or A^(-1) = {pi in A_n : pi(x) in I and pi(I) intersects I is empty}?
justification: The draft matches Green's Problem 4, but Green's comments show that the intended question is an extremal problem about subsets of the alternating group with no internal equation xy=z, not merely a vague request for a large example. Those comments also record the pre-solution state of the art: a Crane-type construction of density about n^(-1/2), and Eberhard's upper bound within a logarithmic factor. The later primary source cited by Green makes the sharp solved formulation explicit: Keevash, Lifshitz and Minzer define the candidate extremal families F_I^x and prove in Theorem 1.1 that, for sufficiently large n, every maximum-size product-free subset of A_n is, up to inversion, exactly one of these families. Therefore the stand-alone formulation should define A_n, product-free, the quantifier over n, and the extremal family F_I^x, and should state the problem as determining the maximum cardinality together with the extremizers.

citations.label: Upper bound on the density of the largest product-free subset of A_n
